soundness_flags.label: def:model-class / def:covariance-class / thm:square-equality / oeq:positive-real-compiler
soundness_flags.one_line: \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\) is called semialgebraic while it includes algebraic independence over \(\mathbb Q\), a countable genericity condition that is not semialgebraic; consequently the chamber/interior and closure predicates defining \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) lack a stated ambient semialgebraic domain.

soundness_flags.label: estimand_functional / target_estimand
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed observed-law functional outputs classes indexed by the unobserved true \(G\) and a compiler \(\mathfrak C_p\) that is itself only the requested OEQ object, without stating the factor-recovery input or quotient under which these are functionals of the context laws.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Definition 3.14 and Theorem 3.15, article HTML lines 605–621; Problems 5.1–5.2, lines 763–771
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 3.14 defines soft(G) through baseline inverse-path rank equalities, Theorem 3.15 equates that class with its compatibility notion, and Problems 5.1–5.2 ask for a combinatorial description and covariance-versus-soft strictness.
The paper studies a linear transformation of a linear latent causal model and states that one intervention on each latent variable suffices for identifiability using a partial-order RQ decomposition.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 4, Theorems 1–2 and discussion following Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under its faithfulness assumptions the paper identifies the latent causal model up to its CD-equivalence class and discusses prediction of unseen intervention combinations.
Trek separation characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank constraints for directed graphical models.
The half-trek criterion is a polynomial-time-checkable sufficient condition for generic identifiability of linear SEM parameters.
The latent-factor half-trek criterion supplies an effective sufficient criterion for rational identifiability and is polynomial-time checkable when latent search sets are bounded.

source_verification_receipts.version: Preprint corresponding to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 66 (2020)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops semidefinite tests for latent causal structures, furnishing the cited convex-certificate comparator rather than a coupled soft-LCD branch-union result.
The result gives implicit semialgebraic descriptions under a birational map with positive denominators and is framed for globally rationally identifiable models.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Separate a genuinely semialgebraic positive-support parameter space from the Zariski-generic locus; state every closure, relative interior, and chamber relative to that former space, with a finite theorem-specific exceptional-polynomial list replacing algebraic independence.

Make the estimand conditional on explicitly recovered aligned factor matrices, or add a precise cumulant-identifiability hypothesis and define the output as a permutation-invariant observable-law functional; remove the not-yet-constructed compiler from the estimand.

Promote the fork eight-branch classification to the mandatory first proved deliverable, including explicit branch equations and a nonsingular open collision or full-dimensional separator, before claiming a general compiler route.

recommended_next_step: Revise the parameter-space and observable-functional definitions, then retain the actual-row and positive-real compiler program as a field-tier Stage-0 target.
